$comment: Single source of truth for the kun keyword vocabulary. Edit THIS file, then run: node .claude/scripts/generate-vocab.mjs — it regenerates the Vocabulary block in .claude/CLAUDE.md and src/components/docs/spellbook-data.ts. health.sh runs generate-vocab.mjs --check to flag drift. v2 (2026-07-10): deduped cross-school keywords, retired stale BMAD spells, wired Anthropic-native automation (loop/goal/schedule/workflow). Spell fields: name (the keyword), effect (one-line), order (routing chain: familiar=agent, portal=MCP, skill=/skill-or-command, hook, ward=rule, memory), steps, connects, depends, and optional mergedInto (keyword retired into another).

schools.name: The Pipeline
schools.subtitle: Idea to production in one word
schools.description: The most powerful magic in Kun. Each keyword is a complete pipeline stage. Chain them with `feature` to go from idea to customer's hands in minutes.
schools.quote: feature billing hogwarts — one line, eight stages, live in production.

spells.name: feature
spells.effect: Chain all pipeline stages — idea to production
steps: IDEA: Create structured GitHub issue with acceptance criteria
SPEC: Data model sketch + file plan + refined criteria
PLAN: Architecture decisions — patterns, mirror target, tradeoffs
TASKS: Dependency-ordered work list on the issue
SCHEMA: Prisma model + migration + Zod validation
CODE: Server actions with auth + validation + tenant isolation
WIRE: Pages + forms + tables + i18n wired to actions
WATCH: Post-deploy health check + issue closed

spells.name: idea
spells.effect: Capture a feature as a structured GitHub issue
steps: Parse feature name + optional product scope
Read product context: existing pages, models, components
Generate structured body: user story, acceptance criteria, scope

spells.name: spec
spells.effect: Technical specification — data model, file plan, human approval
steps: Survey codebase: schema, routes, components, product CLAUDE.md
Design: Prisma model sketch, file plan, refined acceptance criteria
Publish spec as comment on the issue
PAUSE: Human approves before implementation begins

spells.name: plan
spells.effect: Architecture plan from the approved spec — patterns, tradeoffs, risks
steps: Read the approved spec from the issue
Choose patterns: mirror target, pattern cards, data flow
Append the plan as a comment on the feature issue

spells.name: tasks
spells.effect: Dependency-ordered task breakdown from the approved plan
steps: Read the plan from the issue
Order by dependency; mark parallelizable work
Publish the checklist on the issue

spells.name: schema
spells.effect: Prisma model + migration + Zod validation schemas
steps: Create Prisma model with relations and tenant isolation
Create Zod validation schemas + TypeScript types

spells.name: ready
spells.effect: Pre-code readiness gate — validates spec, schema, and dependencies
steps: Check spec exists on issue with acceptance criteria
Check schema is migrated and types compile
Check dependencies are resolved (no blocking issues)
Check Definition of Ready checklist is met
Verdict: PASS / CONCERNS / FAIL with reasons

spells.name: code
spells.effect: Server actions with auth + Zod validation + tenant scoping
steps: Read schema and types from previous stage
Create server actions: create, list, get, update, delete
Each action: auth check → Zod validate → Prisma query → revalidate
Create authorization rules (RBAC if product uses it)

spells.name: wire
spells.effect: Pages + forms + tables + i18n — the layer users see
steps: Create form.tsx (client, React Hook Form + Zod + server actions)
Create columns.tsx (table column definitions if list view)

spells.name: check
spells.effect: Quality gate — type-check + build + visual verification
steps: Navigate to page with browser → screenshot → verify renders
Report: all gates green or list failures

spells.name: ship
spells.effect: Commit + push + deploy to Vercel production + verify
steps: Stage and commit with conventional message + Closes #N
Poll deployment status until Ready (max 10 min)
If Error: fetch logs, diagnose, fix, redeploy (max 3)

spells.name: watch
spells.effect: Post-deploy health check — confirm customer can use it
steps: Quick smoke test: click primary action, verify
If clean: close feature issue with summary

spells.name: report
spells.effect: Auto-fix user-reported issues — read, verify, fix, close
steps: Session start: check open report issues across all repos
READ: gh issue view → extract page URL + description
LOCATE: URL → route directory (src/app/) + component directory (src/components/)
CONTEXT: read CLAUDE.md, README.md, ISSUE.md for the feature
VALIDATE: real bug? aligned with plans? safe to fix?
SEE + DEBUG: screenshot page, check console errors, network failures
IDENTIFY: correlate report + visual + errors → root cause
FIX: edit minimum code in component directory
BUILD: pnpm build — verify no regressions
PUSH: conventional commit (fix: ...) + push to main
VERIFY: see the page again after deploy
CLOSE: close issue with fix summary

spells.name: approve
spells.effect: The human gate — the review queue on /social/publish approves in-app, or a signed one-click link reaches a remote approver; either way it ends by stopping
steps: Assemble copy + media per channel, exactly as it will appear
Pre-flight: Arabic glyphs, no text baked into a render, AI media labelled, consent for faces
Primary lane — the review queue on /social/publish: load the next answered full draft, fine-tune, Approve (claims answered → consumed, then publishes now or schedules to the drain) or Dismiss
Remote lane — stageForReview: one pending variant + one 12h signed link per channel (never /api/social/relay: it publishes immediately); staging retires the queue entry so no draft is approved twice
STOP. Deliver the links and wait; the gate never times out into a publish
Record the decision per channel — approved, held, dismissed, or rejected

spells.name: publish
spells.effect: The review queue decides, the lanes deliver — approved full drafts drained where an API exists, copy-out where none does
steps: /social/publish is a REVIEW QUEUE, not a composer: next-up draft, browse the rest, fine-tune, never create from blank
Verify the gate — refuse without a recorded approval (request consumed), a pending variant with a live link, or a human yes in-session
Partition by lane: DRAIN (telegram, facebook), HERMES (gateway pulls), MANUAL (whatsapp)
Drain lane: Approve now, or approve-mode schedule / --at writes scheduled variants for /api/social/drain (~15 min, 3 retries)
Media routes by shape: text · one photo · 2–10 album/carousel · one video; mixed kinds refused by name
Manual lane: render the copy-out block for a human to forward; never mark it published
Record externalId per channel, then log the slot back to /calendar

spells.name: social
spells.effect: One spell — calendar, draft, media, approve, publish, measure for a brand post. Eight distribution channels reach an audience; Slack is the one internal channel
steps: Pre-flight: resolve the brand and its wired DISTRIBUTION_CHANNELS; refuse Slack as a destination and say why
Stage 1 /calendar — pick the slot from pillars.json (skipped when the topic arrived as an argument)
Stage 2 /draft — the FULL draft: Arabic-first core piece, platform-native variants, and its media set
Stage 3 media — pick from library.json first; generate only on a miss (/higgs text-free, /carousel text-bearing), then attach; a failure downgrades to a text post, it does not stop the chain
Stage 4 /approve — HARD STOP. The review queue on /social/publish is the primary gate; a signed link covers a remote approver. No human yes, no publish, ever
Stage 5 /publish — drain lane (now or scheduled), hermes lane, or a copy-out block for whatsapp

Art-direct (optional): push templates to Figma (writes are quota-free) or the claude-design canvas; hosted Figma pulls respect the 6-read budget
Stage for human approval — deliver slides + captions and STOP; no approval, no publish

After approval: Telegram album via scripts/post-to-telegram.mjs --media; IG/FB from the exported files; LinkedIn takes the PDF; log to the calendar

spells.name: record

schools.name: The Owlery
schools.subtitle: Lead acquisition and outreach
schools.description: Hogwarts' owls carry post out and bring the reply back — which is the whole job here, and the reason this school is named for delivery rather than for discovery. Measured 2026-08-17, the CRM's 3,156 school leads break down as 176 contactable, 13 with a Facebook page, 32 with a website, and 2,935 that are an OpenStreetMap name and a map pin with no online handle at all. So automated enrichment caps at +45 rows and a full scrape run adds +15, while 131 tier-A/B schools are contactable and unworked today. Every spell here makes contact-gap analysis, enrichment and outreach the easy path and raw discovery a deliberate choice someone made out loud. Arabic forms are first-class — half this work is Arabic. Code lives in hogwarts/scripts/crm/ and mkan/scripts/crm/ (canonical); kun holds the routing and none of the scrapers.
schools.quote: "scrap facebook for hogwarts" — and the owl comes back with thirteen pages, not three thousand. Knowing that before you send it is the spell.

schools.name: The Floo Network
schools.subtitle: Conversation to conversion
schools.description: The Floo Network is the one magical transport where you must say the destination clearly or you arrive somewhere random — which is the entire thesis of this school. The CRM holds 3,156 school leads and has converted none of them, so every number here starts at zero on purpose: 0 funnel sessions, 0 gates instrumented, 0 active paying schools against a Q3 2026 target of 1. hogwarts already HAS the chatbot (Groq, bilingual, mounted on both the SaaS site and every tenant site) and it captures nothing; the inbound Prospect plumbing is written and has zero importers. So the work is not building a bot — it is making the one we have ask the seven questions a sale requires, segment on the answers, give value before asking for money, and never let a lead go quiet without a smart next touch. The funnel logic is deterministic and costs zero tokens per lead; the LLM only ever drafts follow-up copy in batches on the Max pool. Code lives in hogwarts/ and mkan/; kun holds the routing and none of the funnel.
schools.quote: "follow up" — and the lead that went quiet three weeks ago gets a guide it has never seen, not a "just checking in". Every touch carries something new, or it does not fire at all.

One question per gate; a gate missing its question, field, asset or timer is broken

steps: The clock is launchd + Vercel cron, never a Twenty CRON — Twenty is down whenever the Mac sleeps
Touches 1-2 are templated and send unattended; touches 3+ are drafted and need a recorded human yes
Drafting is ONE claude -p session per tick on the Max pool — never one call per lead

Nothing is ever deleted — a deleted row is an outreach history nobody can audit
This mode never sends; sending is follow up, and it is opt-in
